summary: Office VPN DNS resolution failures affecting private repo and internal dashboards
description:
Issue summary: Since ~2026-03-10 09:10 local, several engineers on the SF office VPN report failures resolving internal hostnames (git.redwood.internal, grafana.redwood.local). Impact: A subset of staff cannot git push/pull to internal repos, dashboard lookups fail, and some CI jobs that use internal services are timing out. Scope appears limited to devices on the office VPN (remote users unaffected).

Impact details: ~12 engineers affected intermittently, multiple failed CI runs for internal integration tests, on-call paged for degraded access to internal dashboards. No customer-facing outages.

Environment: Office VPN (on-prem concentrator) -> corporate DNS forwarders -> internal DNS cluster (10.10.0.0/24). Observed from macOS and linux clients; Windows reports are mixed.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Connect to office VPN. 2) Attempt to resolve git.redwood.internal (nslookup/dig). 3) Attempt git clone/pull of small repo. 4) Observe timeouts or NXDOMAIN. Intermittent success if retry after ~30s.

Initial hypothesis: DNS forwarder saturation or misconfiguration causing NXDOMAIN/servfail responses; possible packet loss between VPN concentrator and DNS cluster. Also investigating MTU/path issues that could fragment UDP DNS.

Logs & data collected: - tcpdump from client shows DNS queries sent to 10.10.0.11 but either no response or truncated UDP responses. - VPN concentrator health checks show occasional packet drops on interface eth2 at 2026-03-10T09:08-09:25. - Internal DNS nodes show spike in query rate coincident with the time window.

Temporary mitigation: Engineering recommended switching affected clients to split-tunnel (bypass VPN for git traffic) where permitted; SRE opened a temporary iptables rule to prefer TCP DNS to 10.10.0.12 for affected hosts.

Requested next steps: Triage network path between VPN concentrator and DNS cluster, validate MTU/settings, check for recent firewall changes, and increase DNS worker capacity if load-related.
